    All Classes and Interfaces

    Class
    Description
    Applicative<F>
    A Functor that can lift plain values and combine independent Fs.
    ApplicativeError<F,E>
    An Applicative that can fail with an E and recover.
    Async<F>
    Can wait for a callback-based computation, such as a client library's completion handler.
    Bracket<F,E>
    A MonadError that can guarantee clean-up: acquire, use, release whatever happens.
    CallableK<A>
    A Callable<A> as a Kind<Callable, A>.
    Concurrent<F>
    Can run Fs at the same time: start fibers, race them, run them in parallel.
    ConcurrentEffect<F>
    An effect that is both Concurrent and Effect: it can be run, and what runs can start fibers, race and run in parallel.
    Derives
    Asks the forj plugin to derive type class instances for a record: what record User(long id, String name) derives Codec { } compiles to.
    Effect<F>
    An Async effect that can also be run: the top of the ladder for code that is handed an F and has to produce a value, such as a server running a request's F<Response> on that request's virtual thread.
    Either<L,R>
    A value of one of two types: Left by convention for failure, Right for success.
    Either.Left<L,R>
     
    Either.Right<L,R>
     
    Extension
    Marks a static method as an extension method: what extension <A> String show(A a) compiles to.
    Fiber<F,A>
    A running F started with Concurrent.start(Kind): wait for it or cancel it.
    Foldable<F>
    Can reduce the values inside an F to one value, left to right.
    For
    What forj comprehensions compile to.
    Functor<F>
    Can transform the values inside an F: the bottom of the capability ladder.
    FunctorFilter<F>
    A Functor that can drop values: what guard(...) in a comprehension needs.
    Given
    Marks a type class instance: what given T name = ...; and given <A> T name(using ...) { ... } compile to.
    Implicits
    Scala's summon: Implicits.<Ordering<Integer>>summon() returns that given.
    Instances
    Type class instances for JDK types.
    Instances.CallableInstances
    Callable is a lazy effect that can be run (Effect), but not Concurrent and not FunctorFilter (a guard has nothing to drop).
    Instances.ListInstances
     
    Instances.OptionalInstances
     
    IO<A>
    A lazy, re-runnable description of a computation that may perform side effects, fail, or wait: cats-effect 2's IO, on virtual threads.
    IO.IOConcurrent
     
    Kind<F,A>
    F applied to A: how forj writes a higher-kinded type such as "some F<A>" where F is itself a type parameter.
    Language
    Opt-in language features, switched on per file with a static import, like Scala's import scala.language.implicitConversions:
    ListK<A>
    A List<A> as a Kind<List, A>.
    Lower
    Marks how to turn a Kind<W, A> back into the type it stands for, e.g.
    Monad<F>
    An Applicative whose next step can depend on the previous result: what forj comprehensions need.
    MonadError<F,E>
    A Monad that can fail with an E.
    Monoid<A>
    A Semigroup with an identity: combine(empty(), a) is a.
    OptionalK<A>
    An Optional<A> as a Kind<Optional, A>.
    Par
    Parallel combinators for Callable, in the spirit of cats-effect's parMapN and parTraverse.
    Par.Function3<A,B,C,R>
     
    Par.Function4<A,B,C,D,R>
     
    Semigroup<A>
    A way to combine two As into one; must be associative.
    Sync<F>
    Can suspend side effects: delay(() -> println(...)) describes the print, doesn't do it.
    Syntax
    Extension methods for the type classes, like cats' syntax imports: fa.map(f) on any F<A> with a Functor<F>, a.combine(b) on any A with a Semigroup<A>.
    Traverse<F>
    A Functor and Foldable whose values can be visited with an effect, collecting the results.
    Unit
    The value of effects run only for what they do, like Scala's Unit.
    Using
    Marks a context parameter: what using T name compiles to.
